response.evidence: These figures come from a manual review of the rows, so the counts are approximate. Hispanic or Latino female applicants appear roughly 110 times, with about 14 denials (about 12-13%). The overall denial rate is about 8-9%, and White female applicants are denied at about 9-10%. The gap is small, and with only about 14 denials it could easily be random variation rather than a real pattern. About half of the Hispanic female denials have clear risk factors in the data: debt-to-income of 50% or higher, loan-to-value over 100%, or reported income of 0. Applicants of other races and sexes with those traits (White, Asian and Hispanic male) were also usually denied. Hispanic females were approved at high rates when their profiles were similar to approved applicants, and some with DTI of 50-60% or above 60% were still approved. A few Hispanic female denials (for example, DTI 41-49% with moderate LTV) have no obvious explanation in the data. Comparable unexplained denials also occur for White male and White female applicants. The dataset has no credit score, employment, or lender information, so discrimination cannot be ruled out. However, the data does not show a clear disparity beyond what the recorded risk factors explain.
